answer: An optical scintillation protocol curbs Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to ambient wavefront fluctuations. A verifier challenges nodes to stream real-time phase nonces correlated against references at a coastal jetty, a mountain glacier, and a windblown willow grove. An attacker must finance and operate discrete photonic hardware per identity rather than virtualizing endpoints. However, heavy fog can scatter optical signals, falsely rejecting legitimate agents.
